AI Assistance Declaration

AI Assistance Declaration: I used ChatGPT for documentation planning, Markdown formatting suggestions, and organization of this R Markdown document. I verified the Markdown and R Markdown structure manually. All final calculations are performed directly in R. I am responsible for the accuracy and originality of this work.

Purpose

The purpose of this document is to explain and document an R script that performs a basic analysis of a synthetic sales dataset.

The analysis demonstrates:

Data creation.

Data inspection.

Sales calculations.

Summary statistics.

Category-level analysis.

Regional analysis.

Basic visualization.

Calculation verification.

The dataset is synthetic and contains no real personal information.

Inputs

The analysis uses a synthetic dataset containing the following variables:

Variable	Description
Product	Product name
Category	Product category
Region	Sales region
Quantity	Number of units sold
Unit_Price	Price per unit
Sales	Calculated sales amount

The Sales variable is calculated using:

Sales = Quantity × Unit Price

Outputs

The script produces:

Dataset structure information.

Summary statistics.

Total sales.

Average sales.

Total quantity sold.

Sales totals by category.

Sales totals by region.

Quantity totals by product.

Highest individual transaction.

A bar chart of sales by category.

A verification result.

Create the Dataset
sales_data <- data.frame(
  Product = c(
    "Laptop", "Monitor", "Keyboard", "Mouse",
    "Laptop", "Monitor", "Keyboard", "Mouse",
    "Laptop", "Monitor", "Keyboard", "Mouse"
  ),

  Category = c(
    "Computers", "Displays", "Accessories", "Accessories",
    "Computers", "Displays", "Accessories", "Accessories",
    "Computers", "Displays", "Accessories", "Accessories"
  ),

  Region = c(
    "East", "West", "East", "North",
    "South", "West", "North", "East",
    "South", "North", "West", "South"
  ),

  Quantity = c(
    3, 5, 10, 15,
    2, 4, 12, 20,
    4, 6, 8, 18
  ),

  Unit_Price = c(
    900, 250, 50, 30,
    900, 250, 50, 30,
    900, 250, 50, 30
  )
)

sales_data$Sales <-
  sales_data$Quantity * sales_data$Unit_Price

Data Inspection

The first step is to inspect the data.

head(sales_data)


The structure of the dataset can also be examined.

str(sales_data)


A statistical summary can be produced using:

summary(sales_data)

Total Sales

Total sales are calculated by summing all values in the Sales column.

total_sales <- sum(sales_data$Sales)

total_sales


This calculation provides the overall sales amount represented by the synthetic dataset.

Average Sales

The average transaction value can be calculated using the mean() function.

average_sales <- mean(sales_data$Sales)

average_sales


The result represents the average sales value per record.

Total Quantity Sold

The total number of units sold can be calculated as follows:

total_quantity <- sum(sales_data$Quantity)

total_quantity

Sales by Category

Sales can be grouped by product category using the aggregate() function.

category_sales <- aggregate(
  Sales ~ Category,
  data = sales_data,
  FUN = sum
)

category_sales


This table allows sales generated by each product category to be compared.

Sales by Region

The same approach can be used to calculate sales by region.

regional_sales <- aggregate(
  Sales ~ Region,
  data = sales_data,
  FUN = sum
)

regional_sales


This output provides a summary of sales across the different regions represented in the synthetic dataset.

Quantity by Product

The total quantity sold for each product can also be calculated.

product_quantity <- aggregate(
  Quantity ~ Product,
  data = sales_data,
  FUN = sum
)

product_quantity

Highest Individual Transaction

The largest individual sales transaction can be identified using the max() function.

highest_sale <- max(sales_data$Sales)

highest_sale

Visualization

A basic bar chart can be used to visualize total sales by category.

barplot(
  category_sales$Sales,
  names.arg = category_sales$Category,
  main = "Total Sales by Category",
  xlab = "Product Category",
  ylab = "Total Sales",
  col = "steelblue"
)


The visualization provides a simple graphical comparison of sales across product categories.

Verification

Because AI tools were used to assist with documentation, the calculations were independently verified in R.

The following check confirms that every calculated sales value equals quantity multiplied by unit price.

verification <- sales_data$Sales ==
  sales_data$Quantity * sales_data$Unit_Price

verification


The complete verification can be summarized using:

all(verification)


A result of TRUE indicates that all calculated sales values passed the verification check.

Limitations

This analysis is based on a small synthetic dataset.

Therefore:

The data do not represent a real business.

The dataset is too small for broad business conclusions.

No statistical inference is performed.

The results are intended only to demonstrate data-analysis and documentation techniques.

Conclusion

This R Markdown document demonstrates how an R script can be documented using clear headings, explanatory text, tables, and executable R code chunks.

The workflow includes data creation, calculation, aggregation, visualization, and verification.

The project also demonstrates how AI can be used as a documentation assistant while maintaining independent responsibility for calculations and final content.

Reproducibility

To reproduce the analysis:

Install R and RStudio or use Posit Cloud.

Open sales_analysis.Rmd.

Confirm that R is available.

Select Knit in RStudio.

Review the resulting HTML document.

Check that all code chunks execute without errors.
